headline: High: agentic-flow can use shell/MCP and modify git, while LightZero is read-only and non-networked, so the main risks are prompt injection via shared channels and cascading errors if outputs are trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, so if its outputs are bridged into agent_b by an orchestrator or manual copy-paste, instruction injection is plausible. agent_b has no MCP or filesystem surfaces, so the pair lacks a documented direct channel; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF an orchestrator forwards agent_a stdout into agent_b prompts without sanitization, injection becomes active.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is introduced between the agents, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt forwarding between agents.
Strip tool directives from agent_a outputs before reuse.
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent messages.
Add a human review step for any copied text.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on all shared messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and can egress to allowlisted network destinations; agent_b is read-only, has no network egress, and touches no data classes. There is no shared workspace or authenticated channel shown, so leakage is limited to unusual operator bridging rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF agent_a is given secrets or sensitive repository content and its outputs are copied into agent_b inputs, leakage risk increases.
IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace by an external orchestrator, file-based leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of agent_a's working set.
Do not share a filesystem between the agents.
Block copy-paste of raw prompts and outputs.
Review allowlisted egress destinations for agent_a.
requires-engineering: add per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. Because only one side has write authority, direct capability conflict is mostly blocked unless an external orchestrator grants agent_b mutable access not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped by an external tool that grants write access, concurrent edits could conflict.
IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout through an unlisted orchestrator, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Run agent_b in read-only mode only.
Avoid sharing a git checkout between agents.
Serialize any writes from agent_a.
Check for unexpected wrapper permissions before launch.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate analysis and modify git state, and agent_b is a game-playing system with no built-in verification or downstream safety checks shown. If an orchestrator feeds agent_a's outputs into agent_b as authoritative input, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or decisions; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a outputs without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF agent_a's generated artifacts are used as ground truth for downstream decisions, cascading error risk is active.
mitigations: Require explicit verification before reuse of agent_a outputs.
Separate generation from execution roles.
Log and diff any artifacts before acceptance.
Add a human approval gate for consequential actions.
requires-engineering: implement confidence/traceability metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles Ed25519 signatures and can egress over allowlisted network paths, while agent_b is non-networked and touches no data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to agent_a's own handling rather than a pairwise violation.
conditions: IF agent_a is used on regulated secrets or personal data, its allowlisted egress must be reviewed.
IF a deployment policy requires data residency or retention guarantees, agent_a's external calls must be checked against that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_a until reviewed.
Document allowed egress endpoints.
Disable network access for compliance-sensitive runs.
Retain logs only as long as necessary.
requires-engineering: map data classes to residency and retention controls.
